Vote - AcceptText - Probably right but a second opinion is needed. || lin5 => <:<:Κυρακά̣λῃ|alt|Κύρᾳ κα̣λῇ:>=BL 12.61||ed||κ̣υ̣ρᾷ Κα̣λῇ=BL.9.74|Ἱ̣ε̣ρακά̣λῃ:> || lin15 => φυλακῇ] <:[τῆς] [αὐτῆς(?)] [πόλεω]ς=BL 12.61|ed|[τῆς πόλεω]ς:> … <:[τούτ]ο̣υ̣ς̣=BL 12.61|ed|[αὐτ]ο̣ὺ̣ς̣:> | The suggestion recorded in BL X 51 cannot be confirmed and need not be recorded.

Submit - In l. 2, instead of ὑπ̣α̣τ̣ε̣[ί]α̣ς, a better reading is ὑπ̣α̣τ̣ί̣α̣ς, which is in fact the slightly preferred spelling in the Arsinoite. Cf. -ει- in βασιλείας, θειοτάτου (l. 1) and παρειλή̣φ̣[αμεν (l. 15), and cf. further -ατι- in στρατηλατίσσῃ (l. 4) and -τι- in Πατερμοῦτιν (l. 11). Part of the vertical hasta of iota is visible where the lower curve of epsilon is to be expected. Below that, one can spot the lower end of iota, with a short Häkchen to the right as elsewhere in the papyrus. The relatively wide space between iota and alpha reoccurs in βασιλείας (l. 1).
